title: CORD: Low-Latency, Bandwidth-Efficient and Scalable Release Consistency via Directory Ordering
problem: In multi-processing-unit systems (CPU-GPU, multi-GPU) using write-through cache coherence with release consistency, the source processor must serialize write ordering through itself to the LLC directory, generating unnecessary round-trip communication that increases latency, interconnect traffic, and energy for producer-consumer AI/ML workloads.
motivation: Write-through accesses are prevalent in AI/ML producer-consumer communication patterns, and source-ordered release consistency creates a scalability bottleneck as the number of processing units grows and all-to-all communication intensifies.
method: CORD moves the responsibility for enforcing write ordering from the source processor to the last-level cache directory (the central component that keeps track of which caches have copies of data). Instead of the processor sending each write and waiting for directory acknowledgment, the directory accumulates writes and enforces their ordering locally, eliminating this round-trip communication. To keep memory overhead low, the protocol uses metadata compression (a way to store tracking information in less space) for in-flight writes at the directory and scales across multiple directories without serialization bottlenecks.
key_novelty: Moving release consistency enforcement from the source processor to the cache directory, eliminating unnecessary round-trip communication.
contributions: CORD protocol that shifts write-through release ordering from source to LLC directory
Compact metadata scheme minimizing directory storage overhead for ordering traffic
Scalable multi-directory design without serialization across directories
24% average performance improvement and 13% traffic reduction vs. source ordering with <1% area/power overhead

metrics.speedup: 24% average performance improvement over source ordering
metrics.other: 13% average traffic reduction; 3% overhead vs. hand-optimized message-passing

limitations: Evaluation is simulation-based (gem5) and real hardware validation on multi-GPU systems is not performed.
primary_theme: directory-ordered release consistency for multi-PU systems
